strategy.summary: Send the ball around the outside of the bumper group until you score a goal. Then skim the lit center bumper repeatedly before a side lane resets it.

quickInfo.name: A-B skill shot
quickInfo.summary: A lights the two yellow bumpers, B lights the two red bumpers, and collecting both opens the right-outlane gate.

quickInfo.name: Goal progress
quickInfo.summary: The A and B lanes give three puck advances, while bumpers, center rollovers, and side lanes also advance the puck.

quickInfo.name: Center bumper
quickInfo.summary: A goal lights the center bumper for 1,000 until a Start At Center Ice side lane begins the next goal sequence.

quickInfo.name: Center post
quickInfo.summary: Either upper standup raises the post between the flippers, but the white rollover above the post lowers it.

quickInfo.name: Ball reset
quickInfo.summary: Goal progress, bumper lights, the outlane gate, and the center post reset for each ball.

steps.text: Plunge the top A or B lane and note which pair of colored bumpers lights.
If the ball returns up top, collect the other letter to open the right-outlane gate.
Shoot through the gap outside either outer bumper instead of driving into the center of the bumper group.
Use upper play to advance the puck until the game awards a goal.
Confirm that the center bumper is lit for 1,000.
Shoot the edge of the center bumper so the ball continues into upper play.
Repeat center-bumper edge hits while the 1,000 light remains on.
If a Start At Center Ice side lane turns the light off, rebuild the next goal through the outside gaps.

fallback.title: Outside-gap upper play
fallback.when: Use this plan when direct center-bumper shots rebound toward the drain or the center bumper is not lit.

steps.text: Stop direct shots at the center bumper.
Choose the outside gap that gives the safer upper-playfield return.
Send the ball through that gap to collect puck advances and incidental upper-standup hits.
Use the same route until a goal lights the center bumper.
Return to edge shots only after the center bumper is lit.

alternatives.title: Raised-post control
alternatives.when: Use this plan when an upper standup is available without a direct rebound and the center post is down.

steps.text: Hit either 1,000-point upper standup to raise the center post.
Track the ball past the white rollover that lowers the post.
Use the raised post to recover a center feed without making a rushed flip.
Resume the goal route after the ball reaches a controlled flipper.
Collect A or B on the plunge.
Use outside-gap upper play to advance the puck.
Score a goal to light the center bumper for 1,000.
Skim the bumper edge to continue upper action.
Repeat until a side lane starts the next goal sequence.

techniques.name: Outside-gap upper feed
techniques.instruction: Aim just outside an outer bumper. Use the open path instead of hitting the bottom of the bumper group.

techniques.name: Center-bumper edge shot
techniques.instruction: Hit the side of the lit center bumper. Let the rebound continue toward the upper playfield.

techniques.name: Nudging
techniques.instruction: Read the speed of each descending ball before it reaches a sling. Use a small legal nudge only when it improves the expected kick.

cautions.issue: A shot into the bottom of a bumper can rebound directly toward the center drain.
cautions.response: Use the outside gaps for the build. When the center bumper is lit, aim at its edge instead of its underside.

cautions.issue: Either Start At Center Ice side lane turns off the 1,000-point center bumper after a goal.
cautions.response: Do not chase a side lane during the lit window. Return to goal-building play only after the reset occurs.

cautions.issue: The white rollover above the flippers lowers the center post without warning from the ball's position alone.
cautions.response: Read the post before every center feed. Do not depend on a save after the ball crosses the white rollover.

checkBeforePlay: Confirm Williams Olympic Hockey, ball count, right-gate behavior, center-post behavior, and replay conversion.
Test the five bumpers, outside gaps, side lanes, upper standups, white rollover, and tilt.
strategy.simpleOverview: Olympic Hockey advances a puck through the gaps outside the bumper group until a goal lights the center bumper for 1,000. Plunge A and B to light the colored bumpers and open the right-outlane gate, score a goal through upper play, then skim the lit center bumper repeatedly before a side lane starts the next sequence.
strategy.overview: Olympic Hockey advances a puck through the gaps outside the bumper group until a goal lights the center bumper for 1,000. Collect both top letters when possible, keep the ball outside the bumper group until a goal scores, then graze the lit center bumper so the ball returns upstairs. A Start At Center Ice side lane ends that collect and begins the next goal cycle.
machineSetup: Confirm Williams Olympic Hockey, ball count, right-gate behavior, center-post behavior, and replay conversion.
Test the five bumpers, outside gaps, side lanes, upper standups, white rollover, and tilt.
